title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds automated defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, new quantization profile registry and selector, and unit-economics tooling (autotune CLI + dashboard hooks). Backwards-compatible; runtime switches gated behind feature flags.
description:
Motivation: Customers running production workloads repeatedly ask for predictable unit economics and lower per-token cost without sacrificing latency SLAs. This PR implements an end-to-end automation flow: sensible defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, a curated set of quantization profiles with runtime selectors, and a simple unit-econ autotune tool that suggests model + config combos and emits diagnostics to the Console.

What this changes: 1) Runtime: default batching/caching parameters are introduced (continuous-batching target=64ms, max_batch_size heuristics per-model), safer cache eviction policy and prefix-KV warmup, and an API hook for per-customer overrides. 2) Quantization: new quantization_profile registry (q4_0, q8_0, q4_1-opt) and an RPC for runtime to select the cheapest compatible profile given latency budget. 3) Autotune tooling: a new CLI command `redwood autotune` that runs short perf experiments, computes per-token unit cost, and suggests a winning config; results are posted to the Console as a diagnostic (json blob + metrics link). 4) Tests & docs: unit and e2e tests for the selector, integration tests for cache warmup, and docs + quickstart for the autotune flow.

Compatibility / migration: defaults are opt-in via feature flag `cost_autotune_defaults` (enabled for target beta customers). Existing deployments continue to use configured values. Quantization profiles are additive; models without profiles fall back to current behavior.

Benchmarks: on internal standard RLHF inference load (median seq 128, tail 512) we observe ~22% reduction in token cost with 5% median latency regression at P95 which is within our latency SLO for the target bucket. For high-latency-tolerant workloads we see up to 35% savings by selecting q4_1-opt + aggressive batching. Full benchmark appendix attached in commits.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime changes implemented and unit tested - [x] Quant profile registry + selector implemented - [x] Autotune CLI + Console hooks - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs and quickstart - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan

discussion: Samir Patel (reviewer) \u0014 2026-02-21: Nice end-to-end. A couple questions: 1) How do we ensure q4_1-opt correctness on long-context workloads? 2) Can we expose a per-route opt-out?

Ava Chen (author) \u0014 2026-02-21: Responses: 1) q4_1-opt includes additional FP fallback for attention kernels when seq_len>1024; we added a compatibility check in profiles.rs to skip that profile. 2) Yes \u0014 the runtime accepts per-route policy via route config and the CLI emits a route-level recommendation. Added docs section.

notes_for_ops: Feature flag `cost_autotune_defaults` off by default. Rollout plan: enable for internal beta customers for 2 weeks, monitor unit-econ dashboard (autotune/summary), then ramp to 25% of hosted traffic. If P95 latency increase > 10% for any tenant, automatic rollback rule triggers.
post_merge_actions: 1) Run `redwood autotune --dry-run` in benchmark-lab for top-10 models; 2) Create dashboard group 'Unit Econ / Autotune' (owner: CostOps); 3) Add Linear task ENG-1129 to collect customer feedback
benchmarks_summary: Internal benchmark (rlhf-std): median cost -22%, P95 latency +5% (within SLO). Aggressive config (q4_1-opt + batch target 128ms) yields -35% cost for latency-tolerant routes. Full CSVs attached in commit c9e7a21.
user_impact: Primarily internal tooling and platform behavior; customers in beta will get automated suggestions. No breaking API changes. Admins can opt out per-route or per-tenant.
